instruction: Please change VLC's progress slider colors to a dark/blackish theme. I prefer darker interface elements.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task asks user to change slider colors to blackish tones (qt-slider-colours in vlcrc). The evaluator uses existing check_qt_slider_colours metric with type='blackish' to verify all color RGB values are below threshold (100). Similar complexity to original task - both involve modifying VLC's visual appearance settings.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Instruction requires changing slider colors to dark/blackish theme, and evaluator checks qt-slider-colours setting with blackish validation
Correct state extraction: Getter (get_vlc_config) correctly reads VLC config file (vlcrc) containing slider color settings
Correct comparison logic: Metric (check_qt_slider_colours) parses color string into RGB tuples and validates all RGB values < 100 threshold, which is semantically correct for 'blackish' colors
Proper parameter handling: Metric correctly accesses rule['type'] directly without incorrectly accessing expected.get('rules')
Appropriate postconfig: Restarting VLC ensures config changes are loaded and testable
Practical feasibility: All components can execute successfully at runtime - getter can read vlcrc, metric can parse and validate color values
